bss.topic: Constituição de 1988: cidadania, direitos e deveres

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é uma Constituição?
options: A lei mais importante de um país, que organiza o Estado e garante direitos
Uma lista de compras do governo
questions.answer: A lei mais importante de um país, que organiza o Estado e garante direitos
questions.hint: Todas as outras leis precisam respeitá-la.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi promulgada a Constituição brasileira atual?
questions.hint: Ela tem o ano no próprio nome: "Constituição de ...".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como a Constituição de 1988 ficou conhecida?
questions.hint: O apelido tem a ver com cidadania e direitos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Constituição de 1988 foi feita logo depois de qual período da história do Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi um período em que muitos direitos e liberdades foram limitados.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem escreveu e votou a Constituição de 1988?
options: Uma Assembleia Nacional Constituinte, formada por representantes eleitos
questions.answer: Uma Assembleia Nacional Constituinte, formada por representantes eleitos
questions.hint: Os representantes foram escolhidos pelo voto do povo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um DIREITO garantido pela Constituição?
questions.hint: Direito é algo que a pessoa pode receber ou exigir.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um DEVER do cidadão?
questions.hint: Dever é uma responsabilidade que a pessoa precisa cumprir.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Constituição diz que todos são iguais perante a lei. Isso significa que:
options: as leis valem para todas as pessoas, sem discriminação
cada pessoa faz a sua própria lei
questions.answer: as leis valem para todas as pessoas, sem discriminação
questions.hint: Pense na palavra "igualdade".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o nome do regime em que o povo escolhe seus governantes pelo voto?
questions.hint: A palavra vem do grego e quer dizer "governo do povo".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Segundo a Constituição, a partir de quantos anos o voto é permitido (opcional) no Brasil?
questions.hint: É dois anos antes da idade em que o voto se torna obrigatório.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Para quem o voto é OBRIGATÓRIO no Brasil?
options: Só pessoas com mais de 70 anos
questions.hint: Para jovens de 16 e 17 anos e idosos acima de 70, o voto é opcional.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Constituição divide o poder em três. Quais são eles?
questions.hint: Um governa, outro faz as leis e outro julga.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual poder tem a função principal de fazer as leis?
questions.hint: "Legislar" quer dizer criar leis.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que significa ser cidadão?
options: Ter direitos e deveres e participar da vida da sociedade
questions.answer: Ter direitos e deveres e participar da vida da sociedade
questions.hint: Cidadania não depende de onde a pessoa mora.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a Constituição de 1988 é considerada um marco da democracia no Brasil.
questions.hint: Pense no período que veio antes dela e nos direitos que ela garantiu.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Dê um exemplo de um direito e de um dever que fazem parte do seu dia a dia e explique cada um.
questions.hint: Pense na escola, na rua e em casa.

en.topic: Synonyms, antonyms and shades of meaning

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a synonym of 'big'?
questions.hint: A synonym means the same or nearly the same.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is an antonym of 'ancient'?
questions.hint: An antonym means the opposite.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is an antonym of 'generous'?
questions.hint: Think of someone who does not like to share.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which group of words is ordered from weakest to strongest?
questions.hint: Imagine the temperature rising.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word best shows someone is VERY angry?
questions.hint: Look for the most intense shade of meaning.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: 'The old man ___ along the path, leaning on his stick.' Which verb fits best?
questions.hint: Think about how a tired, elderly person might move.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which pair are NOT synonyms?
questions.hint: Look for the pair with opposite meanings.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word has a more positive tone: 'slim' or 'skinny'?
questions.hint: Which would you rather be called?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word has a negative tone?
questions.hint: Which one sounds like criticism?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Add a prefix to make an antonym of 'possible'.
questions.hint: Try im-, un- or dis-.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Add a prefix to make an antonym of 'agree'.
questions.hint: Try un-, dis- or im-.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A thesaurus suggests these synonyms for 'walk'. Which is best for a soldier on parade?
questions.hint: Think of regular, firm steps in time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why should you be careful when choosing a word from a thesaurus?
options: Synonyms can have different shades of meaning
Every synonym means exactly the same
questions.answer: Synonyms can have different shades of meaning
questions.hint: Think about 'slim' and 'skinny'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: 'The child was terrified.' Which word would make the feeling WEAKER?
questions.hint: Look for the mildest feeling of fear.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'The dog was thin' and 'The dog was scrawny'.
questions.hint: Think about the picture and feeling each word creates.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite 'It was a nice day' using a more precise word than 'nice', and explain why your word is better.
questions.hint: Think about the weather, light or feeling you want to show.

en_read.topic: Gothic and ghost stories: building atmosphere

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a typical setting for a gothic story?
questions.hint: Gothic stories like dark, mysterious places.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'atmosphere' mean in a story?
options: the mood or feeling of a place
questions.answer: the mood or feeling of a place
questions.hint: It is how a scene makes the reader feel.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which weather is most often used to create a gothic atmosphere?
questions.hint: Think of dark and dramatic weather.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence builds suspense best?
options: Slowly, the door creaked open, and something moved in the shadows.
She opened the door and went in.
questions.answer: Slowly, the door creaked open, and something moved in the shadows.
questions.hint: Look for details that make you want to know what happens next.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the word for the feeling of excitement or worry about what will happen next in a story?
questions.hint: It is a keyword for this topic.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sense is the writer using in 'A cold, damp smell of earth filled the cellar'?
questions.hint: Which part of the body notices this detail?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is a common feature of gothic stories?
questions.hint: Think about ghosts, secrets and strange happenings.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why might a writer use short sentences in a scary scene?
options: To speed up the pace and build tension
questions.answer: To speed up the pace and build tension
questions.hint: Short sentences feel quick, like a racing heartbeat.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In 'The Canterville Ghost', what is funny about the family who move into the haunted house?
options: They are not frightened of the ghost at all
They run away on the first night
questions.answer: They are not frightened of the ghost at all
questions.hint: The joke is that the haunting does not work.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In 'The Canterville Ghost', how does the ghost feel when his tricks fail?
questions.hint: Imagine trying to scare someone who just laughs.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How is a humorous ghost story different from a traditional one?
options: It turns the reader's expectations upside down
It never has a ghost in it
It is always set at the seaside
It has no setting at all
questions.answer: It turns the reader's expectations upside down
questions.hint: We expect a ghost to be scary…

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word best describes a 'foreboding' feeling?
options: a sense that something bad will happen
a feeling of being very hungry
questions.answer: a sense that something bad will happen
questions.hint: Fore- means before.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: 'The candle flickered and went out.' What effect does this have?
options: It makes the scene darker and more mysterious
It shows the room is warm
questions.answer: It makes the scene darker and more mysterious
questions.hint: Think about what happens when the only light disappears.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is an example of personification that adds atmosphere?
options: The wind moaned through the empty halls.
questions.answer: The wind moaned through the empty halls.
questions.hint: Look for the wind doing something a person does.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Write one sentence describing a haunted house that uses at least two senses.
questions.hint: Think about what you can hear, smell or feel, not only see.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think writers of ghost stories often set them at night?
questions.hint: Think about what darkness does to what we can see and imagine.

en_spell.topic: Latin roots: aqua, port, struct, spect

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: What does the Latin root 'aqua' mean?
questions.hint: Think of an aquarium.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: What does the Latin root 'port' mean?
questions.hint: Think of something portable.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: What does the Latin root 'struct' mean?
questions.hint: Think of a structure.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: What does the Latin root 'spect' mean?
questions.hint: Think of a spectator.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word from this week's list means 'a tank where fish are kept'?
questions.hint: It contains the root for water.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'able to be carried easily'?
questions.hint: Port + able.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'a person who watches an event'?
questions.hint: It uses the root that means look.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.hint: Think of de- + struct + -ion.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: con_ _ _uct (to build)
questions.hint: The root for build is s-t-r.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: a_ _atic (living in water)
questions.hint: The root for water starts with a-q-u.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: What does 'export' mean?
options: to carry goods out of a country
questions.answer: to carry goods out of a country
questions.hint: Ex- means out; port means carry.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word does NOT belong in the 'port' word family?
questions.hint: Check which root each word contains.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'carrying people or goods from one place to another'?
questions.hint: Trans- means across.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: akwatic → aquatic; spectater → spectator; distruction → destruction; inspeckt → inspect
questions.hint: Check each word with a Latin root.
questions.text: At the aquarium, our class watched the akwatic animals. A spectater asked how the tanks were constructed. The guide said the structure is very strong to stop any distruction. Later, we helped to inspeckt a portable tank that is used to transport baby turtles.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: exsport → export; construkt → construct; strucure → structure; enspect → inspect; akwarium → aquarium
questions.hint: Look for the roots port, struct, spect and aqua.
questions.text: Our town builds boats to exsport all over the world. Workers construkt each boat with a strong strucure. A safety officer comes to enspect every one. They are then put on a big ship for transport, and visitors can watch from the spectator deck like a giant akwarium.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling of the word meaning "to look at closely" is correct?
questions.hint: in + spect.

ipc.topic: Investigators — Entry point: a crime scene mystery

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is 'evidence' in an investigation?
options: information that helps show what happened
questions.answer: information that helps show what happened
questions.hint: Investigators collect it at the scene.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What does 'forensic' science do?
options: uses science to help solve crimes
questions.answer: uses science to help solve crimes
questions.hint: It is used by crime scene investigators.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is a hypothesis?
options: a final answer that is always true
questions.hint: It often starts with 'I think… because…'.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why do investigators wear gloves at a crime scene?
options: So they do not leave their own fingerprints
questions.answer: So they do not leave their own fingerprints
questions.hint: They must not change the scene.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why are no two people's fingerprints the same?
options: Each person's ridge pattern is unique
questions.answer: Each person's ridge pattern is unique
questions.hint: Look closely at the lines on your fingertip.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which is an observation, not an opinion?
options: There is a muddy footprint by the window.
The thief was probably very rude.
This is the worst crime ever.
questions.answer: There is a muddy footprint by the window.
questions.hint: An observation is something you can see or measure.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why should investigators photograph the scene before touching anything?
options: To record exactly how it looked
questions.answer: To record exactly how it looked
questions.hint: Once things are moved, the original scene is lost.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which of these is a scientific question an investigator could test?
options: Does the soil on the shoe match the soil in the garden?
Is the suspect a nice person?
What is the thief's favourite colour?
questions.answer: Does the soil on the shoe match the soil in the garden?
questions.hint: Look for a question you can answer with a test or comparison.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What word describes using your senses to notice details carefully?
questions.hint: It is one of this week's keywords.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: A footprint is 30 cm long. Suspect A has 30 cm shoes and Suspect B has 24 cm shoes. What can you conclude?
options: Suspect B probably did not make it
questions.answer: Suspect B probably did not make it
questions.hint: Compare the sizes.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is chromatography used for in an investigation?
options: separating inks to see if they match
questions.answer: separating inks to see if they match
questions.hint: Think about a note written in pen.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why should evidence be put in sealed, labelled bags?
options: To keep it clean and know where it came from
To hide it from the police
To make it look tidy for photographs
questions.answer: To keep it clean and know where it came from
questions.hint: Contamination could ruin the evidence.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What makes a test fair?
options: Changing only one thing at a time
Guessing the result first and not testing
questions.answer: Changing only one thing at a time
questions.hint: Keep everything else the same.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which tool helps you look closely at a tiny hair found at the scene?
questions.hint: It makes things look bigger.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: A window is broken and there is glass on the inside floor. What does this suggest, and why?
questions.hint: Think about which way the glass would fall.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Plan how you would find out which of three pens was used to write a mystery note.
questions.hint: Think about a fair test and what you would compare.
